exercise.name: Assisted Bulgarian Split Squat

reference.title: Assisted Bulgarian Split Squat
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Suspension trainer (straps from an overhead anchor)

breathing.pattern: Inhale on the way down, exhale on the way up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s down, short pause, about 1.1 s up

prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbells, a pause at the bottom, then a front-foot deficit. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.
prescription.load: Body weight with help from the straps; use less help to make it harder.

cues.text: Laces of the back foot on the bench, front foot about a leg length ahead; hold the suspension-strap handles in front of the chest with the straps taut.
Breathe in and drop the back knee straight down; the arms straighten a little on the straps and help you balance and lower.
Front thigh about parallel to the floor, chest tall, straps still taut.
Breathe out and drive through the whole front foot to stand up; pull on the straps only as much as you need.
Stay in the stance and repeat; then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Front foot too close to the bench
mistakes.fix: Move it forward until the front shin is near vertical at the bottom and the heel stays down.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing hard through the back foot
mistakes.fix: The back foot only balances; the front leg does the work.
Keep the knee over the 2nd-3rd toe.

mistakes.mistake: Toes curled under on the bench
mistakes.fix: Rest the laces flat on the bench so the ankle stays relaxed.

kinematics.setup: 45 cm flat bench, rear ankle 3 cm past its near edge
kinematics.peak: Rear foot (laces) stays on the pad
kinematics.norm: About knee height, 40-50 cm is common (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Stance length (front ankle to bench edge)
kinematics.setup: 84 cm between ankle centres (87 cm from the bench edge to the front ankle; rig leg length 90 cm hip to floor)
kinematics.norm: About one leg length from the rear support (common coaching); about one leg length was suggested as optimal in the split squat (Song 2023)
About 90 degrees with the front thigh near parallel (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: ≈104°, 18.9 cm above the floor (knee joint centre)
kinematics.norm: Drops toward the floor; the rear foot stays on the bench (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 1.8 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.1 s up, 1.0 s reset
kinematics.norm: About 2 s down, 1 s up (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: One anchor 222 cm high, 70 cm in front of the shoulders; handles at chest height
kinematics.peak: Strap length 129.8-129.9 cm over the loop (taut); handles turned -62.7° in the hand
kinematics.norm: The straps take some body weight and help balance; using less help makes the legs work harder (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Assisted Bulgarian Split Squat, video (movement reference)
Helme, Emmonds & Low 2022, is the rear foot elevated split squat unilateral? An investigation into the kinetic and kinematic demands (J Strength Cond Res 36(7):1781-1787)
Mausehund, Skard & Krosshaug 2019, muscle activation in unilateral barbell exercises: implications for strength training and rehabilitation (J Strength Cond Res 33(7S):S85-S94)
Song et al. 2023, effects of step lengths on lower-extremity biomechanics during the split squat (Front Bioeng Biotechnol 11:1277493)

cautions: Check the strap anchor and keep both straps taut; let the legs do most of the work.
Set the bench where it cannot slide.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee pain: move the front foot farther forward and shorten the depth.
regressions: Assisted split squat with both feet on the floor.
progressions: Bulgarian split squat without assistance, then with dumbbells.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors do most of the work: the front foot carried about 84% of the vertical force (Helme 2022). Vastus lateralis activity was similar to the split squat and single-leg squat (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors do most of the work: the front foot carried about 84% of the vertical force (Helme 2022). Vastus lateralis activity was similar to the split squat and single-leg squat (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor; gluteus maximus activity did not differ from the split squat or single-leg squat (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor; gluteus maximus activity did not differ from the split squat or single-leg squat (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Biceps femoris activity was higher than in the split squat (76% vs 62% MVIC), giving the highest hamstring-to-quadriceps ratio of the three exercises (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Biceps femoris activity was higher than in the split squat (76% vs 62% MVIC), giving the highest hamstring-to-quadriceps ratio of the three exercises (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension on the front leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension on the front leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Holds the pelvis level on the narrow front-foot base; it was less active than in the single-leg squat (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Holds the pelvis level on the narrow front-foot base; it was less active than in the single-leg squat (Mausehund 2019).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall and the pelvis square to the front.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright as it tips slightly forward.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright as it tips slightly forward.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: The rear-leg hip flexors are stretched as the hips drop (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: The rear-leg hip flexors are stretched as the hips drop (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steady the shoulders while the arms hold the straps.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Steady the shoulders while the arms hold the straps.

phases.label: Rear foot on the bench, dumbbells at the sides
